# ESP32-C6 upstream refresh A/B at kixel-ai/rind `8a5977ad`

Interleaved A/B of five fork branches against upstream [kixel-ai/rind](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind) main [`8a5977ad`](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/commit/8a5977adb9c32ea2ed010c400f5ffbdcdec14b47) on one ESP32-C6, 2026-11-23. The tables below are the control image, six flashes. [ab.md](ab.md) has every image against the control, [RUNS.md](RUNS.md) every control run, and [NOTES.md](NOTES.md) the method and what each image is.

- Board: ESP32-C6 rev v0.2, 4 MB flash, USB-Serial/JTAG; the board whose MAC ends 2C:48
- CPU: Espressif ESP32-C6 (RISC-V riscv32imac), 160 MHz
- Toolchain: rustc 1.98.1 (nixpkgs), riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf, opt-level 3, lto fat, codegen-units 1
- Control image `ctl`: kixel-ai/rind main 8a5977ad as it is (HACL* ChaCha20 rounds and 64-byte keystream array, HACL* Poly1305 in u64 limbs, aws-lc bitsliced AES, 64-bit-product GHASH, 6-bit P-256 table, byte-at-a-time volatile key wipe)
- Control runs: 6 flashes (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 of 11)

## rind against the fastest other library (control image)

Below 1.00× rind is faster. Spread is (slowest − fastest run) over the median, for rind and for the fastest other library. The only other library in this firmware is RustCrypto (ed25519-dalek for Ed25519).

## Images against the control

[ab.md](ab.md): each candidate image (`zero`, `aes`, `p256`, `cp`, `all`) was flashed once, between two control flashes. One flash is one run, so the candidates do not meet the three-run rule; see [NOTES.md](NOTES.md).
